answer: An agent economy can require each identity to pass a periodic, randomized live challenge — a proctored task drawn from fresh entropy — where steady participation forges an onyx-hard trust record. Crossing the ridge from newcomer to trusted takes dozens of successful rounds, and a failed or skipped challenge drops the identity back into the umber haze of the unverified. Sybils must therefore keep many identities continuously doing real work instead of cheaply spinning up fakes, making each extra identity linearly costly in compute and attention rather than free.
